items.statement: Manufacture every drug in line with the current good manufacturing practice requirements.
items.quote: All drugs must be manufactured in accordance with the current good manufacturing practice regulations

items.statement: Keep records relating to prescription drugs readily available for FDA review.
items.quote: Records relating to prescription drugs must be readily available for review

items.statement: Comply with all drug CGMP requirements, including record requirements, for both prescription and over-the-counter drugs.
items.quote: all manufacturers of prescription and OTC drugs must comply with the drug CGMPR requirements, including those involving records

items.statement: Have a quality control unit that holds the responsibility and authority set out in the CGMP regulations.
items.quote: The firm must have a quality control department that has the responsibility and authority as described in the referenced CFR.

items.statement: Keep the quality control unit independent of the production department.
items.quote: The quality control department must maintain its independence from the production department

items.statement: Set out the responsibilities of the quality control unit in writing.
items.quote: its responsibilities must be in writing

items.statement: Document the training each employee has received.
items.quote: The training received by an employee should be documented.

items.statement: Have quality control perform an annual product review for each drug manufactured.
items.quote: Quality control must do product annual review on each drug manufactured

items.statement: Have written procedures for the annual product review.
items.quote: have written annual review procedures

items.statement: Include in the annual review a summary of all lots that failed in-process or finished product testing, and of other critical factors.
items.quote: The report should provide a summary all lots that failed in-process or finished product testing, and other critical factors.

items.statement: Investigate any failures.
items.quote: Investigate any failures.

items.statement: Have quality control validate the manufacturing process for each drug manufactured.
items.quote: Quality control must validate the manufacturing process for each drug manufactured.

items.statement: Provide adequate lighting, ventilation, screening and proper physical barriers for all operations, including dust, temperature, humidity and bacteriological controls.
items.quote: There must be adequate lighting, ventilation, screening, and proper physical barriers for all operations including dust, temperature, humidity, and bacteriological controls.

items.statement: Keep adequate blueprints describing the high purity water, HEPA and compressed air systems.
items.quote: There must be adequate blueprints which describe the high purity water, HEPA, and compressed air systems.

items.statement: Provide adequate locker, toilet and hand washing facilities at the site.
items.quote: The site must have adequate locker, toilet, and hand washing facilities.

items.statement: Provide adequate space for placing equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups in the receiving, sampling and storage of raw materials.
items.quote: receiving, sampling, and storage of raw materials;

items.statement: Provide adequate space for placing equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups in manufacturing or processing.
items.quote: manufacturing or processing;

items.statement: Provide adequate space for placing equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups in packaging and labeling.
items.quote: packaging and labeling;

items.statement: Provide adequate space for placing equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups in the storage of containers, packaging materials, labeling and finished products.
items.quote: storage for containers, packaging materials, labeling, and finished products;

items.statement: Provide adequate space for placing equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups in production and control laboratories.
items.quote: production and control laboratories.

items.statement: Install new equipment properly and make sure it operates as designed.
items.quote: New equipment must be properly installed, and operate as designed.

items.statement: When equipment is changed, assess whether the change requires FDA pre-approval and/or revalidation of the manufacturing process.
items.quote: Determine if the equipment change would require FDA pre-approval and/or revalidation of the manufacturing process.

items.statement: Clean equipment before use according to written procedures.
items.quote: The equipment must be cleaned before use according to written procedures.

items.statement: Document and validate equipment cleaning.
items.quote: The cleaning must be documented and validated.

items.statement: Make sure equipment does not adversely affect the identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug.
items.quote: The equipment should not adversely effect the identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug.

items.statement: Use equipment construction materials that do not react with the drug.
items.quote: The material used to manufacture the equipment must not react with the drug.

items.statement: Make sure lubricants or coolants do not contaminate the drug.
items.quote: lubricants or coolants must not contaminate the drug

items.statement: Construct and locate equipment so that cleaning, adjustment and maintenance are easy.
items.quote: The equipment should be constructed and located to ease cleaning, adjustments, and maintenance.

items.statement: Construct and locate equipment so that it prevents contamination from other or previous manufacturing operations.
items.quote: it should prevent contamination from other or previous manufacturing operations

items.statement: Identify equipment with its cleaning status and its content.
items.quote: Equipment must be identified as to its cleaning status and content.

items.statement: Use equipment of suitable capacity and accuracy for measuring, weighing or mixing operations.
items.quote: Determine if the equipment is of suitable capacity and accuracy for use in measuring, weighing, or mixing operations.

items.statement: Where equipment requires calibration, have a written calibration procedure and document the calibration.
items.quote: If the equipment requires calibration, they must have a written procedure for calibrating the equipment and document the calibration.

items.statement: Have written procedures describing how components, drug product containers and closures are received, identified, stored, handled, sampled, tested, and approved or rejected.
items.quote: They must have written procedures which describe how these operations are done.

items.statement: Where the handling and storage of components is computer controlled, validate the program.
items.quote: If the handling and storage of components are computer controlled, the program must be validated.

items.statement: Make component receiving records traceable to the component manufacturer and supplier.
items.quote: The receiving records must provide traceability to the component manufacturer and supplier.

items.statement: Record in component receiving records the component name, the manufacturer, the supplier if different from the manufacturer, and the carrier.
items.quote: The receiving records for components should contain the name of the component, manufacturer, supplier if different from the manufacturer, and carrier.

items.statement: Also record in component receiving records the receipt date, the manufacturer's lot number, the quantity received and the firm's assigned control number.
items.quote: In addition, it should include the receiving date, manufacturer's lot number, quantity received, and control number assigned by the firm.

items.statement: Use only colors approved for their intended use and declare the required statements on the drug label.
items.quote: Determine if the color is approved for its intended use, and required statements are declared on the drug label.

items.statement: Handle components in line with drug CGMP, including components used in the research and development lab.
items.quote: Components must be handled in accordance with the drug CGMP's including components used in the research and development lab.

items.statement: Identify components after receipt and hold them in quarantine until released.
items.quote: Determine how components are identified after receipt and quarantined until released.

items.statement: Identify components so their status (quarantine, approved or rejected) is known.
items.quote: Components must be identified so the status (quarantine, approved, or rejected) is known.

items.statement: Have adequate component sampling and testing procedures and an adequate process for releasing approved materials for use, and follow them.
items.quote: Review the sampling and testing procedures for components, and the process by which approved materials are released for use. Decide if these practices are adequate and followed.

items.statement: Keep a valid and accurate inventory system for drug components, containers, closures and labeling.
items.quote: Determine the validity, and accuracy of the firm's inventory system for drug components, containers, closures and labeling.

items.statement: Investigate significant discrepancies in inventory records.
items.quote: Significant discrepancies in these records should be investigated.

items.statement: Show that containers and closures are compatible with the product, adequately protect the drug against deterioration or contamination, are not additive or absorptive, and are suitable for use.
items.quote: Evaluate the following to determine whether the firm has shown that the containers and closures are compatible with the product, will provide adequate protection for the drug against deterioration or contamination, are not additive or absorptive, and are suitable for use:

items.statement: To show containers and closures are compatible, protective, not additive or absorptive and suitable, have specifications for containers, closures, cotton filler, desiccant and similar items.
items.quote: Specifications for containers, closures, cotton filler, and desiccant, etc.

items.statement: To show containers and closures are compatible, protective, not additive or absorptive and suitable, carry out tests or checks on them (for example cracks, glass particles, durability of material, metal particles in ointment tubes, compliance with compendial specifications).
items.quote: What tests or checks are made (cracks, glass particles, durability of material, metal particles in ointment tubes, compliance with compendium specifications, etc.).

items.statement: To show containers and closures are compatible, protective, not additive or absorptive and suitable, have cleaning procedures for containers and control how containers are stored.
items.quote: Cleaning procedures and how containers are stored.

items.statement: Review the labeling on preprinted containers for accuracy.
items.quote: The firm must review the labeling for accuracy.

items.statement: Have each critical manufacturing step performed by a responsible person and checked by a second responsible person.
items.quote: Each critical step in the manufacturing process shall be done by a responsible individual and checked by a second responsible individual.

items.statement: Where critical processing steps are controlled by automatic mechanical or electronic equipment, verify the equipment's performance.
items.quote: If such steps in the processing are controlled by automatic mechanical or electronic equipment, its performance should be verified.

items.statement: Document critical manufacturing steps at the time they are performed, not before or after the fact.
items.quote: These manufacturing steps are documented when done, and not before or after the fact.

items.statement: Label all containers and equipment used to manufacture a drug at all times.
items.quote: All containers and equipment used in to manufacture a drug should be labeled at all times.

items.statement: Show on the label of containers and equipment their contents, including batch number and stage of processing.
items.quote: The label should identify the contents of the container or equipment including the batch number, and stage of processing.

items.statement: Remove previous identification labels from containers and equipment.
items.quote: Previous identification labels should be removed.

items.statement: Handle and store the batch so as to prevent mix-ups or contamination.
items.quote: The batch should be handled and stored to prevent mixups or contamination.

items.statement: Have adequate in-process controls to ensure product uniformity and integrity, for example checking tablet weights and disintegration time, liquid fill, adequacy of mixing, homogeneity of suspensions and clarity of solutions.
items.quote: To ensure the uniformity and integrity of products, there shall be adequate in-process controls, such as checking the weights and disintegration time of tablets, the fill of liquids, the adequacy of mixing, the homogeneity of suspensions, and the clarity of solutions.

items.statement: Have in-process test equipment on site and perform the specified in-process tests.
items.quote: Determine if in-process test equipment is on site and the specified tests are done.

items.statement: Have personnel check the actual yield against the theoretical yield for each batch manufactured.
items.quote: Determine if personnel check the actual against the theoretical yield of each batch of drug manufactured.

items.statement: Have a procedure that, in the event of any significant unexplained yield discrepancy, prevents distribution of the batch concerned and of related batches.
items.quote: In the event of any significant unexplained discrepancies, determine if there is a procedure to prevent distribution of the batch in question, and related batches.

items.statement: Construct and locate tableting equipment to make maintenance and cleaning easy at the end of each batch, or at suitable intervals for a continuous batch operation.
items.quote: The equipment should be constructed and located to facilitate maintenance and cleaning at the end of each batch or at suitable intervals in the case of a continuous batch operation.

items.statement: Follow the cleaning procedure for tableting equipment.
items.quote: determine if the cleaning procedure is followed

items.quote: To prevent cross-contamination, the mixing, granulation, drying and/or tableting operation should be segregated in enclosed areas with its own air handling system.

items.statement: Make sure parenteral drugs are non-pyrogenic.

items.statement: Avoid any condition in the parenteral manufacturing process that permits bacterial growth.
items.quote: Therefore, any condition that permits bacterial growth should be avoided in the manufacturing process.

items.statement: Train personnel in aseptic procedures.
items.quote: It is important that personnel be trained in aseptic procedures.

items.statement: Make sure employees are properly gowned and use good aseptic technique.

items.quote: Specifications for viable particulates must include provisions for both air and surface sampling of aseptic processing areas and equipment.
